claims_verified: jāmiʿ (3:9:3) is an ACTIVE PARTICIPLE — corpus features 'ACT_PCPL|VF:1|ROOT:جمع|LEM:جامِع|M|NOM'. The identity-vs-event reading is grammatically sound.
3:25 jamaʿnāhum is a finite VERB — 'PERF|VF:1|ROOT:جمع|LEM:جَمَعَ|1P'. The participle/verb contrast is real.
'sixteen ayahs later' — 25 minus 9 = 16. Correct.
3:9 and 3:25 carry the phrase for the Day word-for-word identically: لِيَوْمٍ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ. Verified against corpus text of both verses.
rayba is parsed ACCUSATIVE (3:9:7 'ROOT:ريب|LEM:رَيْب|M|ACC') and لَّا carries 'NEG|FAM:إِنّ' — consistent with lā an-nāfiya li-l-jins, the categorical negation the file describes.

al-Ṭabarī's ellipsis (ḥadhf) reconstruction — VERBATIM in the report: 'وهذا من الكلام الذي استُغني بذكر ما ذكر منه عما ترك ذكره ... ربنا إنك جامع الناس ليوم القيامة، فاغفر لنا يومئذ واعف عنا، فإنك لا تخلف وعدك'. The file's English rendering matches exactly.
al-Jalalayn: mīʿād = مَوْعِده بِالبَعْثِ (the pledged raising of the dead). VERBATIM in source.
al-Jalalayn: 'فِيهِ التِفات عَنْ الخِطاب' (iltifāt away from direct address) — VERBATIM.
al-Jalalayn: 'ويَحْتَمِل أنْ يَكُون مِن كَلامه تَعالى' (the closing clause may be God's own speech) — VERBATIM. The file's most striking move is correctly sourced.
al-Jalalayn: 'أنَّ هَمَّهُمْ أمْر الآخِرَة ولِذَلِك سَأَلُوا الثَّبات عَلى الهِدايَة لِيَنالُوا ثَوابها' — the hamm/ākhira point in Theme Three. VERBATIM.
al-Jalalayn: 'فَتُجازِيهِمْ بِأَعْمالِهِمْ' — the Gatherer also recompenses by deeds (file line 153). VERBATIM.

al-Muyassar: 'ما وَعَدْتَ به عبادك' (promised to His servants) — VERBATIM in report.

claims_false: FALSE — the Quran-wide uniqueness claim. File lines 117-123: 'Search the Quran for this exact formula — lā rayba fīh, with that masculine ending — and it lands on precisely two things ... the Book (2:2, 32:2) ... the Day (3:9, 3:25). That is the whole list.' Exhaustive corpus count: the masculine string لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ occurs 10 times, not 4 — 2:2, 3:9, 3:25, 4:87, 6:12, 10:37, 17:99, 32:2, 42:7, 45:26. Six occurrences are omitted. (The feminine فِيهَا occurs 4 times — 18:21, 22:7, 40:59, 45:32 — all of as-sāʿah, correctly outside the claim.)

FALSE — the categorical version of the same claim ('The Quran spends its most absolute certainty-formula on exactly two objects'). There is a third referent class: 17:99 وَجَعَلَ لَهُمْ أَجَلًا لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ — the formula attaches to an ajal, an appointed term, neither the Book nor the Day. Referent distribution is Book 3 (2:2, 10:37, 32:2), Day 6 (3:9, 3:25, 4:87, 6:12, 42:7, 45:26), ajal 1 (17:99).

FALSE — Theme Four's evidentiary premise. File lines 228-240 title the section 'The Verse the Prophet ﷺ Read with Tears' and claim 'Al-Jalalayn records that both al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmitted via ʿĀʾisha the Prophet's ﷺ profound and deeply moved recitation of these very words — this sequence running through 3:7 to 3:9.' The actual al-Jalalayn text on 3:9 reads: 'رَوى الشَّيْخانِ عَنْ عائِشَة ... تَلا رَسُول اللَّه ﷺ هَذِهِ الآيَة هُوَ الَّذِي أنْزَلَ عَلَيْك الكِتاب مِنهُ آيات مُحْكَمات إلى آخِرها وقالَ: فَإذا رَأَيْت الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ ما تَشابَهَ مِنهُ فَأُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ سَمّى اللَّه فاحْذَرُوهُمْ'. The verse recited is 3:7 alone ('هذه الآية ... إلى آخرها'), not 3:9 and not 'the sequence 3:7 to 3:9'. There are NO tears, no emotion, and no devotional framing in the narration — it is a WARNING against those who chase the mutashābih. The emotional state attributed to the Prophet ﷺ, and sourced to Bukhari and Muslim, is not in the source.
FALSE (minor) — 'We have spent all this time inside fourteen Arabic words' (line 252). 3:9 has 13 words (corpus word indices 3:9:1 through 3:9:13).
issues: The central thesis — the rooted ones, having confessed the limits of their own understanding, close their prayer not with a request but by naming one immovable certainty; jāmiʿ names an identity where 3:25 names an act; the petition is elided (Ṭabarī) and possibly completed from above (Jalalayn's iltifāt + 'may be God's own speech') — is fully corroborated verbatim by al-Ṭabarī, al-Jalalayn and al-Muyassar. This is not a 21:76-77-shaped thesis failure.

But the file carries the SAME defect class that 21:76-77 carried: a Quran-wide exhaustive claim ('that is the whole list') delivered with maximum rhetorical confidence — 'Now count with me, because this phrase has an address' — that does not survive counting. Off by 6 occurrences and by a whole referent class.

Theme Four (≈13 paragraphs, lines 228-243) must be cut or rebuilt. It is not an over-reach on a true source; the source says something close to the opposite of what the file reports, and the file attributes a state of the Prophet ﷺ to the two Ṣaḥīḥs. This is the highest-severity item in either file.

The hadith is genuine and correctly attributed to al-Bukhārī/Muslim via ʿĀʾisha — the fabrication is the CHARACTERIZATION ('read with tears', 'deeply moved', 'overwhelming him', 'not analysis, encounter') and the reference-shift from 3:7 to 3:9.

Ibn Kathir's block in tafsir-report-009.md is filed under heading 3:9 but quotes and comments on 3:7 — an instance of the corpus-wide heading-offset defect. The file did not rely on it, but the report gives no independent Ibn Kathir corroboration for 3:9.

The tafsir report truncates every block at 500 chars (scripts/cross_reference_tafsir.mjs line 131). The al-Jalalayn block is cut exactly at 'تَلا رَسُول اللَّه ﷺ هَذ...' — i.e. the report ends precisely where the hadith's content begins. Whoever wrote Theme Four could not have seen the hadith's actual content in the report and supplied it from memory. This is a systemic trap: the 500-char truncation reliably severs Jalalayn's hadith citations from their content.
summary: Every morphological and structural claim holds, and the load-bearing argument is verbatim-sourced to all three Arabic commentators — this file's thesis is sound. Two separate falsifications sit on top of it. (1) The 'lā rayba fīh attaches to only two things — that is the whole list' claim is false: 10 masculine occurrences, not 4, and a third referent class (ajal, 17:99). (2) Theme Four fabricates an emotional characterization of a Bukhari/Muslim hadith, moves the recitation from 3:7 to 3:9, and titles itself 'The Verse the Prophet ﷺ Read with Tears' — the narration reports no tears and is a warning about those who follow the mutashābih. CRITICAL on (2), which puts an unreported state of the Prophet ﷺ into the two Ṣaḥīḥs.

claims_verified: (a) burūj is the same word used for fortified towers in 4:78 — CONFIRMED. Root برج has 7 tokens; lemma بُرُوج appears 4 times: 85:1, 15:16, 25:61 (all sky) and 4:78 وَلَوْ كُنتُمْ فِى بُرُوجٍ مُّشَيَّدَةٍ (human towers). The file's precise arithmetic — 'in this ayah and two others' for the sky sense, 'once more, in Surah An-Nisa' for towers — is exactly right.

(b) root خدد occurs exactly 2 times in the Quran — CONFIRMED by exhaustive corpus scan: 31:18:3 خَدَّ (LEM خَدّ, cheek) and 85:4:3 أُخْدُودِ (LEM أُخْدُود). No third token. The file's own hedge ('I would not press this as a claim about the Quran's intent; the roots are documented, the resonance is yours to weigh') is exemplary and should be the house pattern.

(c) al-Jalalayn glosses qutila as luʿina — CONFIRMED VERBATIM against the live source: '﴿قُتِلَ﴾ لُعِنَ ﴿أصْحاب الأُخْدُود﴾ الشَّقّ فِي الأَرْض'. This single line also confirms the file's second Jalalayn gloss, ukhdūd = ٱلشَّقّ فِي ٱلْأَرْض.

(d) al-Jalalayn's detail that the watchers sat ON CHAIRS — CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 85:6 '﴿إذْ هُمْ عَلَيْها﴾ حَوْلها عَلى جانِب الأُخْدُود عَلى الكَراسِيّ "قُعُود"'. The file's rendering ('around it, on the edge of the trench — على الكراسي — on chairs') tracks the Arabic word for word.
al-Jalalayn: shuhūd = حُضُور — CONFIRMED VERBATIM at 85:7. (Also independently in al-Ṭabarī in the stored report: 'يعني: حضور'.)

al-Jalalayn on 85:3 shāhid = Jumuʿah / mashhūd = ʿArafah, sourced to hadith — CONFIRMED VERBATIM: '﴿وشاهِد﴾ يَوْم الجُمْعَة ﴿ومَشْهُود﴾ يَوْم عَرَفَة كَذا فُسِّرَتْ الثَّلاثَة فِي الحَدِيث'. The file's phrasing 'passes on a reading from hadith' is accurate.

(e) the ش-ه-د thread — CONFIRMED. Corpus tokens in surah 85: 85:3:1 شَاهِدٍ (ACT_PCPL), 85:3:2 مَشْهُودٍ (PASS_PCPL), 85:7:6 شُهُودٌ (ACT_PCPL, LEM شاهِد, MP), 85:9:10 شَهِيدٌ. The file's grammatical labels — active participle, passive participle, 'the plural of the active participle' for shuhūd — are all correct against the corpus.

(f) the -ūd rhyme — CONFIRMED. Ayah-final words 1-9: بُرُوجِ / مَوْعُودِ / مَشْهُودٍ / أُخْدُودِ / وَقُودِ / قُعُودٌ / شُهُودٌ / حَمِيدِ / شَهِيدٌ. The four the file singles out as locked together — ukhdūd (trench), waqūd (fuel), quʿūd (sitting), shuhūd (watching) — all end -ūd, and the last two do break to -īd as the file says.
quʿūd is a VERBAL NOUN, not a participle — CONFIRMED: 85:6:4 features 'VN|VF:1|ROOT:قعد|LEM:قُعُود|INDEF|NOM'. The file's grammatical point is exactly right.

The load-bearing thesis — the men who took seats at the burning are named with the very root Allah uses for Himself at the close — is textually true (85:7 shuhūd, 85:9 shahīd, both root شهد), and both al-Ṭabarī and al-Muyassar in the stored report support the persecutor-as-spectator reading (Muyassar: 'إذ هم قعود على الأخدود ملازمون له ... حضورٌ').
claims_false: IMPRECISE (not false) — Closing Synthesis: 'Three appearances of the root. Three different agents.' There are 4 tokens of ش-ه-د across 3 ayahs. The body of the file states it correctly ('that root has already appeared, twice, in the oath itself'), so the Closing contradicts the body. Cosmetic, but it is a countable claim stated wrongly.
issues: STRUCTURAL DEFECT — the rebuild is incomplete. Lines 82-96 carry an orphaned block of ayah-9 commentary (the shaheed reveal: 'The watchers were being watched') sitting ABOVE the '## INTRODUCTION' heading, between the translation and the new front half. This is the surviving fragment of the old front-truncated file; the rebuild prepended new material after it instead of removing it. It also duplicates the Closing Synthesis (lines 260-268).

IKHTILĀF SUPPRESSION — the file states 'This is not a report that the trench-people died. It is an imprecation' as settled. The al-Ṭabarī block in the file's own tafsir report (85:4) records the alternative: 'وكان بعضهم يقول: معنى قوله قتل أصحاب الأخدود خبر من الله عن النار أنها قتلتهم' — some read it precisely as a report. And Ṭabarī at 85:6 records Qatāda reading 'إذ هم عليها قعود' as referring to THE BELIEVERS, not the persecutors — which would invert the whole Theme 1 accusation. The file flags ikhtilāf on shāhid/mashhūd but not on the two places where the disagreement bears on its own argument.

THE STORED TAFSIR REPORT IS UNUSABLE and corroborates none of the file's citations. content/tadabbur/085-al-buruj/tafsir-report-001-009.md lists al-Jalalayn as '*Not available for this ayah*' for ALL NINE ayahs — yet al-Jalalayn is in fact available for every one of them (I fetched 85:3, 85:4, 85:6, 85:7, 85:9 live and all five glosses the file cites are verbatim correct). The report also exhibits both defects named in the audit brief: Ibn Kathir's 85:1 buruj block is cloned IDENTICALLY under all 9 headings (and under headings 4-9 it quotes 25:61, an ayah other than its heading), and al-Muyassar's whole-passage block is cloned identically under all 9. So this report is one of the 39% — it should be regenerated, and it should not be treated as having validated anything.

Consequence worth recording: the file's al-Jalalayn attributions are CORRECT but were not verifiable from the artifact on the desk. Whoever wrote them went to the real Jalalayn (or knew it) rather than the report. That is the right outcome here, but it means 'the tafsir validator passed' carried zero evidentiary weight for this file.
summary: All six named rebuild claims verify — several verbatim against the live Tafsir al-Jalalayn, including the two the register leaned on hardest (qutila = luʿina, and the watchers seated عَلى الكَراسِيّ, on chairs). The root counts are exact: خدد is genuinely 2 in the whole Quran, and burūj genuinely spans sky-stations and 4:78's fortified towers. The load-bearing thesis — the spectators are named with the root Allah claims for Himself — is true and well grounded. Downgraded to MODERATE for two things the validators could not see: an orphaned ayah-9 block still sitting above the Introduction (leftover truncation debris that spoils the file's own reveal), and the file presenting qutila-as-imprecation and the seated-ones-as-persecutors as settled when al-Ṭabarī, in the report on the desk, records the contrary readings. Separately, the stored tafsir report for this passage is corrupt (al-Jalalayn missing on all 9 ayahs though it exists; Ibn Kathir and al-Muyassar blocks cloned across every heading) and should be regenerated.
